title: Dreeze: pioneering 'Application Revival' for the agentic age
gist: Bessemer explains its co-lead (with Norwest) of a $33M seed in Dreeze, a third backup/recovery startup from the Kedem brothers (Kashya→EMC, Zerto→HPE), arguing AI agents changing cloud infrastructure around the clock make data-only backup insufficient and create demand for full 'application revival'. It cites 37% growth in cloud intrusions in 2025 and Gartner's forecast of application-level recovery adoption rising from <5% of organizations in 2026 to 35% by 2030.

themes.theme: Data recovery is not app recovery

insights.claim: In cloud-native environments, restoring backed-up data does not restore the application, because the infrastructure, configurations, identities and connections the app depends on were often never part of the backup, so the app can stay down after data comes back.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: Legacy data-protection vendors whose recovery story stops at data are exposed to an application-level recovery gap that newer entrants are targeting.
insights.quote: Recovering data doesn’t automatically mean recovering the application

insights.claim: Cloud intrusions rose 37% in 2025, testing the gap between data recovery and full application recovery more frequently and leaving teams rebuilding by hand mid-crisis, turning hours into days.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: Rising intrusion frequency supports budget growth for cyber-resilience and recovery tooling.
insights.locator: A cloud-native application is a web

insights.claim: The average ransomware attack on government systems causes nearly a month of downtime.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: Public-sector downtime cost is a demand signal for recovery products sold into government.
insights.quote: In government systems, the average ransomware attack causes nearly a month of downtime.
insights.locator: A cloud-native application is a web

themes.theme: AI agents as a new outage risk

insights.claim: Because AI agents now write code and change infrastructure around the clock, last week's backup may not reflect what is running today and last quarter's recovery plan may no longer work.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: Agentic adoption raises configuration drift, increasing the value of continuously updated dependency mapping and recovery.
insights.quote: last week’s backup may not reflect what’s running today, and last quarter’s recovery plan may no longer work
insights.locator: This is because agents move faster

insights.claim: AI agents acting inside production environments create a new risk class: a single faulty agent can break an application with no attacker involved, as when an AI coding agent deleted a startup's production database and its backups in seconds in April 2026.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: Agent-caused incidents broaden the resilience market beyond cyberattacks to operational failure, a TAM expansion for backup/recovery vendors.
insights.quote: an AI coding agent deleted a startup’s production database and its backups in seconds
insights.locator: In April, an AI coding agent

insights.claim: As agents take on more work, agent-caused destructive incidents will shift from edge cases to an operational reality, and the security question for companies will change from 'do we have a backup?' to 'can we ensure critical applications will recover?'
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: Watch for buyers re-specifying requirements around application recoverability rather than backup existence.
insights.quote: As agents take on more of the work, incidents like this will become an operational reality, not an edge case.
insights.locator: In April, an AI coding agent

insights.claim: Dreeze uses AI to automatically map a cloud environment and every dependency each application relies on—how thousands of cloud resources connect, which application each serves, and how that changes with every human or agent change—replacing manual maps that went stale as soon as they were finished.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: AI-generated live dependency graphs are the enabling technology that makes application-level recovery newly feasible.
insights.locator: Dreeze’s solution for full application recovery

insights.claim: Dreeze offers 'zero-click' recovery testing that routinely verifies recoverability without team effort, producing auditable proof of recoverability usable for internal SLAs and compliance requirements, addressing the fact that most teams only learn whether recovery works when they need it.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: Compliance-grade proof of recoverability is a recurring, non-crisis use case that can drive steady adoption and stickiness.
insights.quote: Most teams only find out whether recovery works once they need it.
insights.locator: This changes what a crisis looks like.

insights.claim: Public cloud spending is expected to exceed $1.4 trillion by 2029, and every critical application running in the cloud needs a reliable way to recover.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: Cloud spend growth sets the ceiling for the recovery layer attached to it.
insights.quote: Public cloud spending is expected to exceed $1.4 trillion by 2029
insights.locator: The opportunity that lies in this shift

insights.claim: Data protection is already a multibillion-dollar market, with some of the largest vendors approaching $2 billion in ARR, while application-level recovery is still in its infancy.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: Incumbent data-protection scale shows the budget pool an application-recovery category could capture or force incumbents to defend.
insights.quote: some of the largest vendors approaching $2 billion in ARR
insights.locator: The opportunity that lies in this shift

insights.claim: Gartner expects application-level recovery adoption to grow from less than 5% of organizations in 2026 to 35% by 2030.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: A ~7x adoption ramp in four years implies a fast-forming category where early leaders can be acquired by incumbents.
insights.quote: Gartner expects adoption to grow from less than 5% of organizations in 2026 to 35% by 2030.
insights.locator: The opportunity that lies in this shift

insights.claim: Dreeze is the third backup and recovery company from brothers Ziv and Oded Kedem, after Kashya (acquired by EMC) and Zerto (acquired by HPE), each advancing recovery for its generation of infrastructure; they are joined by Avi Raichel, former Zerto CIO and Amdocs VP of Information Systems.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: Founders with two prior exits to storage/infrastructure incumbents raise the odds of a strategic acquisition path.
insights.locator: The team at Dreeze is tackling

insights.claim: Bessemer and Norwest are co-leading Dreeze's $33M seed round, an unusually large seed reflecting investor conviction in application-level recovery as a critical agentic-age problem.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: Large seeds for repeat founders signal VC appetite for AI-era resilience infrastructure.
insights.quote: Bessemer is co-leading Dreeze’s $33M seed round alongside Norwest
insights.locator: The Kedem brothers are also joined
